title: Task-queue batcher and KV epoch-guard refactor to reduce runtime contention
creator: Priya Desai
description: Background: Over the last 18 months the continuous-batching path has accumulated multiple small synchronization points and ad-hoc prefetch hedges that increase tail latency under mixed workloads. The KV cache uses a coarse-grained lease/eviction protocol (epoch + global lock) that creates cross-core contention when many short-lived sessions compete for slots. This ticket refactors the batcher coordinator to an explicit task-queue model and introduces an epoch-guard layer for KV cache operations to remove the global lock on hot paths. Goals: 1) Reduce 99th-percentile latency for short requests (<=64 tokens) by 25% under mixed load. 2) Eliminate global KV cache lock from token emission fast path. 3) Simplify scheduler state to make future preemption easier. Success metrics: p99 latency, tail jitter, CPU sys-time for runtime threads, and KV cache hit-rate under the standard perf harness. Non-goals: This does not change model-serving semantics, quantization, or network ingress logic. High level approach: - Replace the central continuous-batcher state machine with a bounded task-queue per lane; each task encapsulates a dispatchable minibatch with explicit lifecycle states (queued, admitted, executing, commit-ready). - Move admission control into lightweight per-lane token buckets and a shared, wait-free arbitration ring to avoid central locks. - Implement KV epoch-guards: writers advance per-shard epochs; readers use an optimistic epoch snapshot and fallback linearization if concurrent compaction is detected. - Remove the global KV lease mutex; replace it with epoch checks and compact-on-stall background workers. - Upgrade critical dependencies: bump libaio to 2.8, jemalloc to 5.3 and re-evaluate allocator arenas to avoid cross-thread contention. - Add targeted benchmarks: microbench for KV read/write common case, synthetic p99 token emission workloads, and end-to-end inference runs with our convai and docs benchmarks. Rollout plan: implement behind feature-flag runtime.task_queue_batcher_v1; internal canary in dedicated staging for 48 hours with traffic shadowing, then a 5% production canary routed to dedicated capacity with a fallback to the existing batcher on SLO regressions. Observability: add per-task latency histograms, epoch-stall counters, and a KV cache invariant checker that emits WARN events when eviction rate spikes. QA and testing: unit tests for epoch-guard correctness, stress tests with synthetic hotkey patterns, and chaos tests that inject delays in the compactor. Backwards compatibility: aim for runtime contract compatibility; no changes to external API. Risks: - Regressing throughput under large-batch, long-context workloads due to scheduling overhead. Mitigation: keep existing continuous path available and benchmark against it continuously. - Subtle concurrency bugs in epoch logic. Mitigation: extensive fuzzing + formalize invariants in design doc. Artifacts and references are attached below.
comments: 2025-02-18 - Priya Desai: Created ticket after spike revealed repeated KV lease contention in alpha cluster. Spike notes: https://confluence.internal/redwood/serving/kv-lease-spike (see section 'pooled workload traces').

2025-02-21 - Miguel Alvarez: PoC for task-queue batcher completed. Microbench shows ~12% p99 improvement on 32-core machine for short requests but +4% CPU. Posting draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1284

2025-02-25 - Design review (Liam O'Connor): Concern about memory overhead for per-lane queues. Suggested using a pooled slab allocator and limiting queue depth by admission, not memory. Action: add jemalloc tuning and per-queue soft caps.

2025-02-27 - Research (Chen Wang): Fuzz harness for epoch-guard passes initial 10k randomized ops; one rare schedule yielded a stale pointer deref that was fixed by adding a quiesce check. Patching and re-run.
2025-03-01 - PM sync (Sara Ng): Confirmed rollout plan and SLO gates. Need to add cost estimate for dedicated capacity canary (additional 4 GPUs).

2025-03-03 - Miguel Alvarez: Feature-flag branch created and automated benchmark pipeline wired. Canary job configured in infra: infra/ci/tasks/task_queue_canary.yml. Next step: run 48h shadow canary in staging and collect traces.
